title: Smart City Site Planning using Autodesk Forma Site Design
description:
• Description
• Students are tasked with designing a Smart City using Forma Site Design for effective site design for adding details to the buildings in the site.
• The Site area selected must have minimum 1 km square area
• The goal is to design and develop a site including the contextual data (available for free within Forma Site Design) and export Site BIM model suitable for further use in Revit app.
• The Site designed must include Site Limits, Landscaping, Buildings, and Transportation elements.
• The Site designed must be analyzed using the Analyze functions available within Forma Site Design for Area Metrics, Embodied Carbon, Sun hours, Daylight potential, Wind Analysis, Microclimate analysis, Noise analysis, Solar Energy.
• Minimum 2 Site Design proposals must be compared and presented using the Forma Borad available within Forma Site Design.
• Objective Urban populations continue to grow rapidly, creating the need for smarter, more sustainable, and resilient cities. Planners, architects, and engineers must leverage data-driven design tools to evaluate site performance, optimize land use, and improve the quality of life for future residents.In this project, students are tasked with designing a Smart City Development using Autodesk Forma Site Design for site planning and analysis, and Autodesk Revit for detailed building development.
• Participation Guidelines For Idea Submission:
• Each student team should submit Forma Site Design with 2 proposals that are compared for their and a Forma Site Design PowerPoint presentation (5-7 Slides).
• Models should be created using only Forma Site Design and not copied or taken from any other source.
• AI Generated content is NOT ALLOWED.
For Grand Finale: Students must use Forma Site Design to design, and create 3D Model of specific office building within the given time period and present the following to the jury members:
• PPT explaining the final Site Design proposal
• Detailed and synced drawing block of a building exported, edited in Revit app and then synced to Forma Site Design.
• Presentation of the Proposal Comparison done through Forma Board
• Rendered images and Walkthrough video (30 secs.) of the final Model.
Note: Teams coming with pre-designed files will be disqualified.
• Attach Marking Criteria Table here*
• Faculty (SIH SPOC) Form Teams choosing to submit idea for Autodesk’s problem statement are required to request their faculty (SIH SPOC) to fill this 'Mandatory Form'.
• Autodesk Forma Site Design
• Autodesk Forma Site Design is a complete Site Design and Site Analysis web app built on native Forma AI HUB primarily used by architects, engineers, and construction professionals to design, model, and document the site and present proposal for approvals.
• Educators and Students can download 'Autodesk Forma Site Design'.
• Essential workflow and learning access Click Here to get FREE access to Forma Site Design.
summary: Innovation (3/5): draws on ai applied to a smart automation problem, placing it in the moderate band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Automation. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on model. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 18/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Smart City Site Planning using Autodesk Forma Site Design

overview.in_plain_terms: Design (not code) at least two competing smart-city site layout proposals for a 1-square-kilometer area using Autodesk Forma, then analyze and compare them on real performance metrics like carbon footprint, sunlight, and wind, not just how they look.
overview.why_it_matters: Urban planning decisions have huge, long-term consequences. This challenge tests genuine data-driven site-planning skill, comparing real performance tradeoffs, not just aesthetic layout.
pain_points: Urban site planning often lacks rigorous, data-driven performance comparison between design alternatives.
Planners need tools that quantify tradeoffs (carbon, daylight, wind, noise) not just visualize layouts.
No standard workflow demonstrates comparing multiple site proposals on quantified sustainability metrics.
overview.background: This is an Autodesk-sponsored site-planning design challenge using Forma Site Design, requiring students to design and quantitatively compare smart city site proposals.
overview.whats_being_asked: Design a minimum 1 km² smart city site (limits, landscaping, buildings, transportation) in Autodesk Forma, analyze it across multiple performance metrics (carbon, sun hours, wind, noise, solar energy), and compare at least two proposals using the Forma Board.
expected_solution: Complete site design with limits, landscaping, buildings, transportation.
Multi-metric performance analysis (embodied carbon, daylight, wind, microclimate, noise, solar).
At least two compared site design proposals.
Export-ready BIM model for downstream Revit use.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Design/CAD submission format, evaluated on genuine site-planning quality and data-driven comparison rigor, not software functionality.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Effort goes into real urban site design and using Forma's analysis tools meaningfully, a distinct skillset from coding.

competitive_landscape.level: Low crowding among typical hackathon teams
competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine urban planning/architectural design skill and Autodesk Forma access specifically, a different pool of participants.

innovation.note: Judged on genuine site-planning quality and meaningful use of quantitative analysis tools, not algorithmic novelty.

invention.note: Judged on the depth and genuineness of your multi-metric comparison between proposals.

technical_feasibility.note: Achievable within 36 hours for a team with real Forma/urban-design experience; not achievable without it.

impact_and_benefits.note: About demonstrating genuine data-driven urban site-planning capability.

architecture.note: Not applicable in the software sense, this is an urban design and analysis deliverable.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Same framing as the other Autodesk PS, only viable for a team with genuine architectural/urban-planning design skill and Forma experience specifically.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very clear, well-specified analysis requirements (specific metrics named explicitly: embodied carbon, sun hours, wind, noise, solar) give a rigorous, checkable comparison framework.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Producing two site designs that only differ cosmetically, without a genuine, meaningfully different tradeoff being demonstrated in the analysis, would miss the actual point of the comparison requirement.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Design your two proposals with a genuinely different underlying design hypothesis (e.g. dense mixed-use versus dispersed low-rise), so the quantitative comparison actually reveals a meaningful tradeoff, not just minor layout variation.

idea_0_4: Confirm team Forma/urban-design proficiency; if none, do not pursue this PS.
Choose a real site area (minimum 1 km²) and define two genuinely different design hypotheses to compare.
Split: one person per proposal, working in parallel within the shared site context.
prototype_4_22: Design your first site proposal: limits, landscaping, buildings, transportation.
Design your second, genuinely different proposal.
Begin running Forma's analysis functions on both (carbon, sun hours, wind, noise, solar).
integration_22_30: Complete your full analysis suite for both proposals.
Compile your comparison using the Forma Board.
Identify and document the genuine tradeoffs your analysis reveals between the two approaches.
polish_30_36: Prepare clean visualizations of both site designs and their comparative analysis.
Prepare your presentation explaining your two design hypotheses and what the data-driven comparison actually revealed.
Export your BIM model output as required.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Present a genuine, non-obvious tradeoff your analysis revealed, e.g. one proposal scoring better on solar potential but worse on wind comfort, and discuss the real planning decision that comparison would inform, that's the actual value of data-driven site comparison, not just two pretty renders.

strengths: Very clear, rigorous analysis requirements give a checkable comparison framework.
Real value in demonstrating genuine data-driven urban planning skill.
weaknesses: Completely inaccessible without genuine Forma/urban-design experience.
Easy to produce two superficially different but analytically similar proposals without real design-hypothesis differentiation.

roles_needed: Urban planner/architect with Autodesk Forma experience (mandatory)
team_fit.ideal_ratio: This PS is not viable without genuine Forma proficiency and urban design sensibility.
team_fit.approach: Define genuinely different design hypotheses for your two proposals before modeling, so the comparison has real analytical substance.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Not applicable, this is a design-skill deliverable requiring real hands-on tool experience.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: The entire site-planning design process and genuine interpretation of what the analysis results actually mean for real urban planning decisions.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: Not applicable in the typical sense, but without real design sensibility, the two proposals risk being superficially different without revealing a meaningful, interpretable tradeoff.

data_resource_availability.status: Forma provides free contextual data for site design; no additional dataset needed.

judge_qna.question: What's the genuine design hypothesis difference between your two proposals, not just visual variation?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Explain your two distinct planning approaches clearly (e.g. density distribution, building orientation strategy) and how that design choice is what the analysis is actually testing.
judge_qna.follow_up: Which specific analysis metric most clearly differentiated your two proposals, and why?

judge_qna.question: How would you actually use these analysis results (carbon, wind, solar) to make a real planning decision?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through a realistic decision-making scenario using your specific data, e.g. how the solar and wind results would inform building orientation or landscaping choices in a final design.
judge_qna.follow_up: What additional analysis would you want before finalizing a real site plan?
